entities.summary: Patrick Miller Hemingway was an American wildlife manager and writer who was novelist Ernest Hemingway's second son and the first born to Hemingway's second wife Pauline Pfeiffer. During his childhood he travelled frequently with his parents and then attended Harvard University, graduated in 1950, and, shortly thereafter, moved to and lived in East Africa for twenty-five years. In Tanzania, Patrick was a professional big-game hunter and owned a safari business for more than a decade. In the 1960s, the United Nations appointed Hemingway to the Wildlife Management College in Tanzania as a teacher of conservation and wildlife.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a professional big-game hunter and owner of a safari business in Tanzania, Patrick Hemingway played a significant role in promoting wildlife conservation in East Africa during his 25-year tenure. His appointment to the Wildlife Management College in Tanzania as a teacher of conservation and wildlife had a lasting impact on regional wildlife management practices.
